messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + expansion — term length and capacity uplift

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We’re ready to move forward on the 2027 renewal, but procurement flagged two items we need addressed before routing to legal:

1) Duration: Aurelia would like to move from the current 12-month term to a 24-month term (start 2027-07-01). They prefer a fixed 24-month pricing cadence rather than annual reprice.
2) Capacity: We expect a ~50% increase in peak token consumption starting Q3 (OrderForm attached). Need clear exhibit/ordering language to lock that uplift and associated pricing.

I attached a draft addendum (Aurelia_Renewal_Addendum_v3.docx) and the updated order form. Can your team provide redlines to the MSA and the addendum and confirm whether any SLAs or billing proration will change with the longer term? Also please call out any changes that would affect audit/retention clauses — we are in a regulated line of business.

Target timeline: procurement wants fully executed paperwork by 2027-05-07 so they can align budget. Is that feasible?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Procurement, Aurelia Health
elena@aureliahealth.com

Hi Elena — thanks for the clarity and for the attachments. We can aim for the 2027-05-07 execution target but will need a quick legal pass and a short commercial confirmation on the price locking mechanism. Looping in David (legal) and Kimberly (commercial) to review the addendum and order form.

Quick answers up front:
- Term length: 24-months is workable; David, please highlight any MSA clauses that need explicit change (auto-renewal, termination windows, early termination fees).
- Capacity uplift: we can reflect a committed uplift as an Exhibit; commercial to confirm uplift pricing and proration.
- Audit/retention: David to advise on retention language — Aurelia’s note on regulated workloads is noted.

Can you confirm whether Aurelia requires onboarding credits or a ramp credit for the first two months of the uplift? Procurement mentioned this as a potential ask.

I’ll aim to get redlines back by EOD Monday (05/03) so we can circulate a DocuSign link for signature by 05/07.

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Aurelia renewal — redline approach and sprint plan

Thanks — I reviewed the addendum and the order form. High-level legal notes (see attached MSA redline for exact edits):

1) Term/Auto-renewal: We should accept 24-month firm term, but add explicit non-renewal notice window of 60 days before term end (MSA currently has 30). This protects both sides and matches billing cycles.
2) Early termination: Keep an early termination fee equal to remaining committed spend (standard), but offer a scaled cap (no more than 6 months of remaining committed spend) to be commercially reasonable for Aurelia.
3) Billing/proration: If uplift billing starts partway through a billing month we will prorate on a days-used basis. Call this out in Exhibit A to avoid back-and-forth.
4) Data retention/audit: Replace the generic retention clause with the regulated-workloads addendum language (I added a short paragraph requiring SOC2 evidence upon request and 90-day advanced notice for retention changes).
5) SLA credits: No change to standard SLA; if Aurelia insists on tighter SLOs we’ll need a priced SLA addendum.

Commercial suggestion: offer a one-time ramp credit equal to either $25k or 3% of uplift ARR, whichever is greater, conditioned on signature by 05/07. That should smooth procurement.

I attached: MSA_redline_RK_v1.docx (with inline edits), OrderForm_redline_DK.xlsx (pricing table updates).

If that approach is OK I’ll finalize the redline and Rachel can send to Elena with a DocuSign link.

-David
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Capacity uplift: Committed +50% uplift is captured in Exhibit A (OrderForm_redline_DK.xlsx). Billing for the uplift will be prorated on a days-used basis if it begins mid-month.
- Early termination: Standard early-termination language remains but with a cap (no more than 6 months of remaining committed spend) to mitigate downside risk.
- Audit/retention: Added language to support SOC2 evidence requests and a 90-day notice for changes to retention policy.
- Ramp credit: Commercial is prepared to offer a one-time ramp credit of $25,000 on the first invoice, contingent on execution by 2027-05-07.
